I diagnosed the problem class and built a working, verified solution.

## Deliverable

- **`/workspace/solution.md`** — the full markdown solution (title, root-cause analysis, exact fix with complete source, verification evidence, soundness notes).
- **`/workspace/wasm_alias_verifier.py`** — the dependency-free verifier (1,406 lines).
- **`/workspace/test_verifier.py`** — 12-case verification suite.

## Root cause

The four named threats share one root cause: the checker must reason about **wrapping machine-integer address arithmetic, aliasing over one flat memory, a growing page budget, and indirect targets simultaneously** — while a naive checker reasons locally and enumerates paths. Local checks miss wraparound (guard holds, `base+width` wraps), views (rights are per-view, enforcement is per-byte), `memory.grow` (static `mem_min` snapshot), and `call_indirect` (table entries can be mistyped/disallowed). Path enumeration is exponential/infinite on loops.

## Fix

A **sound abstract interpretation** over the structured AST:
- value domain = interval + explicit wraparound bit;
- control flow = branch lattice joins (no path enumeration);
- loops = Kleene fixpoint with **threshold widening** seeded by module constants (precise, terminating);
- path conditions = comparison guards refine branch intervals;
- memory = forbidden set is the complement of permitted regions, per-byte range intersection;
- page-count interval detects `memory.grow` past `permitted_pages`;
- table may-set + signature check detects confused indirect calls;
- unsafe → compact witness trace; safe → proof summary with loop invariants.

## Verification

```text
$ python3 -m pytest -v test_verifier.py
12 passed in 0.05s

safe_bound_check             -> safe
wraparound_add               -> unsafe (wraparound)
forbidden_direct             -> unsafe (forbidden)
memory_grow                  -> unsafe (memory_grow)
indirect_type_confusion      -> unsafe (indirect_call)
overlapping_data_segments    -> unsafe (overlap)
loop_guard_proves_safe       -> safe
loop_without_guard_unsafe    -> unsafe (forbidden)
imported_memory_grow         -> unsafe (memory_grow)
indirect_disallowed_callee   -> unsafe (indirect_call)
```

The loop case proves a bounded `loop` safe with fixpoint invariant `i ∈ [0,100]` without enumerating iterations. I also confirmed the source embedded in `solution.md` compiles standalone under Python 3.12. Everything runs with no third-party dependencies (`wat2wasm` is only used by the test harness).
